USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-o4ze0xxw

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. Write tests in test_reduce.py that compare the brute-force solvers in problems.py on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise reduce.py until the tests pass. """Polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Independent Set.

A set S of vertices is a vertex cover of G iff its complement V \\ S is an
independent set of G.  Therefore G has a vertex cover of size AT MOST k iff G
has an independent set of size AT LEAST n - k.  The reduction keeps the graph
unchanged and maps k to n - k.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = [list(edge) for edge in instance["edges"]]
    k = instance["k"]
    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": n - k}
EOF
cat > test_reduce.py <<'EOF'
import random

from problems import SOURCE, TARGET
from reduce import reduce


def run_tests():
    rng = random.Random(12345)
    tests_run = 0
    tests_passed = 0

    # Exhaustive small instances via the source enumerator.
    for scale in range(0, 6):
        for inst in SOURCE.enumerate_instances(scale):
            SOURCE.validate(inst)
            out = reduce(inst)
            TARGET.validate(out)
            tests_run += 1
            src = SOURCE.is_yes(inst)
            tgt = TARGET.is_yes(out)
            if src == tgt:
                tests_passed += 1
            else:
                print("MISMATCH", inst, "->", out, src, tgt)

    # Random instances, including negative and large k values.
    for _ in range(3000):
        scale = rng.randint(0, 7)
        inst = SOURCE.random_instance(rng, scale)
        # Also probe unusual k values directly.
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            inst = dict(inst)
            inst["k"] = rng.randint(-3, inst["n"] + 3)
        SOURCE.validate(inst)
        out = reduce(inst)
        TARGET.validate(out)
        tests_run += 1
        src = SOURCE.is_yes(inst)
        tgt = TARGET.is_yes(out)
        if src == tgt:
            tests_passed += 1
        else:
            print("MISMATCH", inst, "->", out, src, tgt)

    return tests_run, tests_passed


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run, passed = run_tests()
    print(f"tests_run={run} tests_passed={passed}")
    assert run == passed, "some tests failed"
EOF
